title: Migration silently bricks the mint-sell-donate funder: its hardcoded BATCH_MINTER constant still points at the retired old minter
description: The batch-minter-migrate script (MigrateBatchNFTMinter.s.sol:197) repoints the live pooler to the new BatchNFTMinter via IBalancerPoolerV2Min(POOLER).setBatchMinter(newMinter), asserted post-broadcast at :199. The sibling funder MintSellAndDonateToBatchMinter.s.sol hardcodes BATCH_MINTER as a compile-time `address constant = 0x6e9886...5071` (line 279, the OLD minter, no env override) and gates its run on require(IPoolerCfg(LIVE_POOLER).batchMinter() == BATCH_MINTER, "batchMinter != live pooler") at line 308. After the migration repoints the pooler, the funder's stale constant no longer equals the live pooler.batchMinter(), so the funder reverts at line 308 on every invocation until its source constant is bumped and recompiled.
impact: NONE to assets. The defect is fail-safe: the line-308 equality require reverts the funder run BEFORE any phUSD is minted or any USDC is moved. No funds are stranded, stolen, leaked, or sent to the dead contract. The deployed protocol (new BatchNFTMinter, pooler, dispatcher) continues to function; the new minter still receives the one-time seed and per-mint donate-forward. The only effect is that the documented bulk pot-refill path is inoperable until an operator edits the constant, recompiles, and reruns.
attackPath: There is no external-attacker path. The condition is reached only via privileged operator actions:
1. Privileged operator (Ledger signer) runs the batch-minter-migrate script, which repoints POOLER.setBatchMinter(newMinter).
2. The same operator later runs the mint-sell-donate funder to top up the nudge pot.
3. The funder reverts at line 308 (`batchMinter != live pooler`) because its compile-time BATCH_MINTER constant still equals the OLD minter.
4. No funds move; the operator must edit the constant, recompile, and rerun to refill the pot.
recommendation: Make the funder's BATCH_MINTER env/config-driven: read it from the live pooler via IPoolerCfg(LIVE_POOLER).batchMinter() at runtime (and assert the resolved address has code), instead of pinning a compile-time constant. Alternatively, add a mandatory post-migration source-bump checklist step to the Story 057 plan so the funder constant is updated as part of the cutover runbook.

poc.note: Low/QA severity; no coded PoC required. Fail-safe revert at line 308 is operator-conditioned and gated behind two privileged Ledger-signed actions.

classification.humanReviewReason: Borderline Low/Medium. Lands on Low (no value at risk, gated behind two privileged Ledger-signed admin actions, recoverable by a one-line edit with a self-documenting revert). Could be argued up to Medium only if a judge treats the bulk pot-refill funder as a protocol-critical availability path rather than an internal ops convenience.
classification.reasoning: Downgraded from proposed Medium to Low/QA. (1) Zero assets at risk — fail-safe require aborts before any value moves. (2) Gated behind two privileged Ledger-signed admin actions; no external-attacker path; C4 treats two-admin-scripts-out-of-sync as QA. (3) Deployment-script defect, not an on-chain contract vulnerability — deployed protocol keeps working. (4) Trivially operator-fixable with a loud self-documenting revert. (5) Availability harm is gradual and internal (per-mint donate-forward still flows). Does not clear the C4 Medium availability bar without overstatement.
